transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Ever since my husband’s diagnosis, I feel like I’m reacting to everything in a way I can’t manage, and it’s starting to interfere with how I function at work and at home. It has just gotten to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed, and my primary care doctor suggested I come speak with you.
When was your husband diagnosed, and how long have you been experiencing these overwhelming feelings?

My husband was diagnosed with early-stage Parkinson’s about three months ago. I started feeling this way a few weeks after that, so these overwhelming feelings have been building for about the last two months. It really seemed to start when we began the first big wave of specialist appointments and treatment planning.
Along with feeling overwhelmed, have you been experiencing a persistently sad mood or a loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day?

I wouldn't say I feel a constant deep sadness, but I have completely lost interest and stopped participating in the activities I used to love, like hiking with my group, yoga, knitting, and going to the theater. I just feel too wound up, overwhelmed, and guilty to enjoy any of them right now, so I've completely withdrawn from my usual hobbies.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, or overall energy levels since these feelings began?

My sleep has been terrible because I lie awake running through worst-case scenarios and feel too keyed up to fall asleep properly. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite, but I feel absolutely exhausted all the time from the lack of sleep and constant worry.
Have you found it more difficult than usual to concentrate, focus, or make decisions at work or at home?

Yes, my concentration has slipped significantly, especially at work where I've made avoidable errors on inspection reports that actually led to a tense performance review with my supervisor. At home, I feel too overwhelmed and guilty to focus on or enjoy any of my usual activities like hiking or yoga anymore.
Have you had any thoughts of death, hurting yourself, or that life is no longer worth living?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. Even though I feel incredibly overwhelmed and stressed right now, I've never experienced those kinds of thoughts.
You mentioned feeling guilty; do you also find yourself experiencing deep feelings of worthlessness or feeling like you have failed as a person?

No, I don't feel worthless or like a failure as a person. My guilt is really just about taking any time for myself, like going for a hike or doing yoga, while my husband is dealing with his illness. It just feels wrong to be out enjoying myself when he is going through so much.
Have you or those around you noticed that you are moving and speaking much more slowly than usual, or conversely, that you are extremely restless and unable to sit still?
I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slowly, and nobody has mentioned me being unable to sit still. But internally, I just feel incredibly tense and wound up all the time.

Do these feelings of exhaustion, lack of interest, and difficulty concentrating persist all day, every day, or do they tend to come and go depending on how your husband is doing or what you are focusing on?

They definitely fluctuate and aren't constant all day, usually peaking right after my husband's medical appointments, when I'm struggling to focus on detailed tasks at work, or when I'm lying awake worrying at night. I really hope that once we get through this initial phase and establish a routine with his treatment, these feelings will subside and I can get back to normal.
